analysis.title: Morning Briefing - Blue wave, European ccies outperform, bonds and Gold bid
key_insights: Democrats are projected to win both chambers of Congress. Senate count is Dem 54 - Rep 42 (7 flipped) and House is Dems 227 - Reps 135 (27 flipped). Trump will accept the result and is willing to work with Congress, which removes the risk of court challenges to the ballots and is one reason markets are taking the result in stride.

European currencies, gold and government bonds led overnight. Dollar was broadly offered, with European G10 currencies outperforming the dollar bloc and the yen. SG suggests Ukraine (Democrats lean toward more support) as one explanation.

Democrats take the House and Senate Foreign Affairs Committees. SG expects resumption of US-Iran diplomacy and the oil reaction to become the main market focus. Oil is around $104, the lower end of its 1-month range.

SG says the blue wave should not change the Fed's direction in the short term. A 25bp hike in December remains a high-probability event, and June-27 futures flatten to 55.5bp (-2.5bp). The 2s/10s curve is flat at 33bp.

The Riksbank hiked 25bp to 2.0% after the RBA yesterday and the BoC last week. The statement says further hikes are likely in the coming year. The September path implies 2.3% in 2027 and 2.5% in 2028. The policy rate remains below the neutral range midpoint of 2.25% plus accommodative framing per SG.

SEK is among the top three G10 performers over the past month alongside NOK and CAD, despite negative carry vs the Fed and ECB. EUR/SEK retraced to the 200dma (10.94) after a 11.3665 peak following the late-September Riksbank meeting.
Eurozone October flash CPI is forecast to rise to 4.0% yoy headline (3-year high) with core unchanged at 2.5%. SG says this should seal the next 25bp ECB hike in December.

GBP/USD is at a 7-week high above the 200dma, up 2.7% since the mid-October low. SG attributes this to unwinding of short positions built before last month's Budget. Further gains are possible, which would help the BoE contain inflation.

Brazil COPOM meets today after Lula's surprise election win. BRL is down nearly 10% from 4.98 to about 5.50, Bovespa is down 20% and the 10y BRLGB yield is up more than 250bp to 15.44%. Most economists expect no change today; SG's Dev Ashish expects a cut. USD/BRL resistance is at 5.60/5.63.

SG has become relatively more constructive on BRL vs other LatAm currencies, citing elevated real rates and political risk it thinks is largely priced, since the Lula administration must cooperate with a right-leaning Congress.

Poland's NBP is expected to hold at 3.75% with a hawkish bias. SG now sees +25bp to 4.0% in March. Government-central bank tensions persist, with a coalition vote on suspending Governor Glapinski expected later this month. EUR/PLN hit a 3-year high of 4.4372 earlier this week.

US Treasury refunding is expected to leave auction sizes unchanged but may guide to a possible increase in shorter-dated issuance as early as May. SG economics see greater risk of a government shutdown.
China RatingDog services PMI fell to 50.8 in October from 51.6 in September. The composite fell to 52.0 from 52.4.

Euro rose on short covering. GBP/USD rally reflects unwinding of short positions built before last month's Budget.
geopolitical: Democrats won control of Congress and Trump said he will accept the result and work with Congress.
Democrats control the House and Senate Foreign Affairs Committees, and SG expects US-Iran diplomacy to resume, with oil as the key market channel.
Ukraine: Democrats lean toward more support, and optimism that the frozen conflict could de-escalate would support the euro and lower EGB yields.
Brazil: Lula's surprise election win triggered repricing of Brazilian assets on fiscal concerns.
Poland: tensions between the government and the central bank, including a coalition vote on suspending Governor Glapinski.
